title: SLO-driven partitioned load-shedding proxy for active-active edge
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Our hosted API edge must support active-active multi-region traffic while preserving SLOs for both short synchronous requests and long-lived streaming sessions. During cross-region capacity pressure or partial region outages we currently apply coarse global throttles or brute-force traffic drains that sever streaming sessions and cause user-visible token duplication or loss. This ticket proposes a partitioned load-shedding proxy that enforces SLO-aware shedding at the per-shard (route+tenant+session-type) level, preserves stream continuity when possible, and integrates with circuit breakers and KV-cache hints for graceful handoff.
proposed_solution: Implement a lightweight edge proxy component (slo-proxy) that sits in the gateway path and performs: 1) Real-time SLO budget tracking per route/tenant/cohort using token and latency budgets; 2) Partition-level shedding rules: canary-safe percentage bleed, request-type policies (prioritize sync inference over streaming start events), and session-preserving retries; 3) Circuit breaker hooks to upstream regional pools with exponential backoff and success probes; 4) Streaming resume token issuance and short-lived session tokens to allow safe resume on failover; 5) KV-cache fingerprinting propagated in headers to allow destination replicas to reuse prefix caches where possible. The proxy will expose a /debug endpoint and emit metrics for shed_count, resume_success, circuit_state, and per-cohort SLO headroom.
technical_notes:
- SLO accounting: implement leaky-bucket style budgets keyed by (region, model_variant, tenant_tier, route) with 1s and 1m windows.
- Shedding granularity: support fractional shedding via deterministic hash on request session id to ensure sticky percent of sessions are drained vs preserved.
- Streaming continuity: when deciding to migrate a streaming session, issue a compact resume token that encodes the last consumed kv-checkpoint and a short-lived signature. Upstream runtime will be taught to accept resume tokens and replay cached KV state where available.
- Circuit breakers: integrate with existing region pool health API; use slow-open state to allow occasional probes.
- Safety: default to fail-closed for admin endpoints, fail-open for low-priority routes if explicit SLA says so.
- Backwards compatibility: fall back to current behavior when client doesn't support resume tokens or the upstream runtime can't accept KV hints.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch and unit tests; 2) Deploy slo-proxy behind feature flag in staging for non-streaming routes (2 days smoke); 3) Enable for synthetic streaming sessions with internal clients only (1 week); 4) Gradual ramp to 5% production traffic with simulated region pressure tests (2 weeks); 5) Increase to 25% and then 100% with metrics gating on shed_count, resume_success_rate>98%, and 99th latency within SLOs. Rollback knob: global feature flag + per-region disable API.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for budget calculations and deterministic shedding hashing.
- Integration tests with runtime resume token acceptance and kv-hint path.
- Chaos tests: simulate region capacity drop and verify preserved sessions resume in target region with no duplicated tokens.
- Load tests: synthetic load to assert per-cohort headroom enforcement and that shedding reduces tail latency under pressure.
- Security review for resume token format and short-lived signatures.
acceptance_criteria: SLO budget service emits per-cohort headroom metrics and matches expected token accounting under synthetic load.
Under controlled region degradation, no more than 2% of streaming sessions lose the ability to resume during a 5-minute evacuation for 95th percentile traffic patterns.
Resume token acceptance end-to-end verified with internal runtime: resume_success_rate >= 98% in staged failover tests.
Per-route 99th-percentile latency remains within configured SLO for non-shed traffic at 5% and 25% rollouts.
Circuit breaker transitions and probe behavior observable in telemetry with no cascading fail-open across regions.
Documentation and runbook updated; on-call can disable slo-proxy per-region within 2 minutes.
Security review completed for token signing and header propagation.
risks: Resume tokens might leak sensitive prefixes; ensure tokens are opaque and only contain cryptographic references not raw model state.
Deterministic hashing could concentrate shed decisions on small tenant subsets if session IDs are non-uniform; need fallback randomization seed per-cohort.
Inconsistent KV cache fingerprints between replicas could cause resumption to fall back to cold-start behavior, increasing latency spikes.
Misconfigured shedding rules could inadvertently target high-value enterprise tenants; require explicit tenant opt-in/opt-out configuration.
Rollout complexity: incomplete telemetry could make gating decisions unsafe without adequate dashboards.
